extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary biography, aspiring autobiographers, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative principles for composing an engaging life-narrative or memoir: emphasises honest relation of events, inclusion of feeling, variety of material, moral/instructive purpose, and avoidance of partisan or malicious criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate events with honesty (include accompanying feelings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let him relate the events of his own life with honesty, not disguising the feelings that accompanied them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author should not hide or disguise the feelings accompanying events; honest feeling-reporting renews and deepens reflection, helps readers understand weaknesses with a forgiving eye, and makes a life‑narrative genuinely interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine instruction and amusement / include variety
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective life narrative provides both instruction and amusement and 'has all the charms of variety — high life and low life, vices and virtues, great folly and some wisdom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To interest readers, include diverse material and contrasts (high/low life, virtues/vices, folly/wisdom). Variety keeps a memoir engaging and allows moral or intellectual instruction to be delivered without dullness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sincere self-reflection to deepen moral/psychological insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing one’s life should renew and deepen the author’s reflections on the past and allow readers to view weaknesses without unforgiving or impatient judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memoir should serve both the author's inward work (reflection, correction) and the reader's understanding; sincere self-examination is a virtue in life‑writing and contributes to the work’s educative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with an educative/moral purpose (kindle young minds, guard against scorners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the scheme you advocate (here, Christianity as taught in liturgy and homilies) is in accordance with reason and use the narrative to kindle young minds and guard them against temptations of scorners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a life‑narrative has an explicit moral or doctrinal aim, the writer should demonstrate coherence with reason ('link follows link by necessary consequence') and present faith or belief as a continuation beyond reason’s horizon, using personal example to instruct gently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan or personal animus in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that is a 'rhapsody of predetermined insult' or that shows a political animus (personal/partisan motive) is morally and aesthetically flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and critical writing should aim at impartial appraisal of the work rather than using the review as a vehicle for political hatred or personal attack; partisan motives undermine credibility and can render abuse more telling of the reviewer than useful about the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid designing shallowness and clever craft intended to defame
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not employ a sort of 'designing shallowness and clever craft, artified for the sake of obtaining depreciation, and even of insidious defamation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should not rely on shallow wit or adroit language whose purpose is to belittle or defame; such tactics reveal folly in words and are unethical and unworthy literary practice.
